# A face page that follows events live

<!-- generated by `python -m quality.sdk --reference`; edit the source, never this -->

A face page listens on the tenant's event socket; your services' events arrive there.

## Where the socket is

- **The route** — one consumer at `ws/events/`, under `token_auth(...)`; a product writes none (`apps/realtime/consumers.py:325`)
- **In development** — the face's proxy rewrites `/ws/` to the backend beside `/api/v1/`, so a same-origin socket reaches it (`frontend/next.config.ts:122`)
- **On staging** — Caddy sends every path of the site address to `web:8000`, upgrades included — the same same-origin URL (`deploy/Caddyfile:87`)

```ts
const scheme = location.protocol === "https:" ? "wss:" : "ws:";
const socket = new WebSocket(`${scheme}//${location.host}/ws/events/`);
```

next: who the socket is.

## How it authenticates

- **The session cookie** — a same-origin browser socket carries it; Django's auth stack reads it at the handshake (`config/asgi.py:68`)
- **Or a bearer** — `Authorization: Bearer`, from a client that can set the handshake's header (`apps/realtime/middleware.py:101`)
- **Or a ticket** — a client that cannot set a header mints one with `POST /api/v1/socket-tickets/` and opens `?ticket=` — one use, 60 s; `?token=` is refused, so no credential rides a URL, and the log filter redacts one that tries (`apps/realtime/services.py:29`)
- **Tenant and hat** — `?tenant=<slug>` and `?org=<id>` stand in for `X-Tenant` and `X-Org` (`apps/realtime/middleware.py:85`)

next: what it says.

## What arrives

- **Every event your services emit** — no registration on the socket side: the dispatch workflow pushes each `emit()` after its commit (the worker must be up) (`apps/events/workflows.py:146`)
- **The frame** — an `EventMessage`: `name`, `v`, `payload` (the REST `Out`), `correlation_id`, `organization_id`, `occurred_at` (`apps/realtime/schemas.py:53`)
- **Who hears it** — a socket whose hat may read the event's noun; a noun that is no authorization kind is mapped in your `events.py`'s `EVENT_KINDS`, or its frames are dropped (`apps/core/authz.py:593`)
- **Nothing goes up** — `{"type": "ping"}` gets a pong; anything else closes `4400` (`apps/realtime/consumers.py:541`)

```ts
socket.onmessage = (frame) => {
    const event = JSON.parse(frame.data);
    if (event.name.startsWith("workorders.job.")) refetchJobs();
};
```

next: when it closes.

## Reconnecting

- **A refused handshake is `1006`** — anonymous, or a hat the caller does not hold, is refused before accept; the browser sees `1006` and no code (`frontend/src/api/socket-close.ts:18`)
- **`4410`** — the credential is gone: do not come back with it (`apps/realtime/schemas.py:37`)
- **`4419`** — the session that opened the socket ended: sign in again; a ping does not keep it alive (`apps/realtime/schemas.py:48`)
- **Pushes only** — a frame missed while closed is not replayed: on reconnect, re-read the list over REST (`apps/realtime/consumers.py:1`)
- **The kit** — `useEvents(tenant, kinds)` opens the socket and owns the dial, the backoff, the reconnect and the `4410` close; its `changes` moves on every frame of a kind it was asked for and on every re-open, so a page re-reads when it does (`frontend/src/api/use-events.ts:114`)

```ts
const feed = useEvents(null, ["job"]);
useEffect(() => {
    refetchJobs();
}, [feed.changes]);
```

next: [Events out](events-out.md), for naming and emitting the events.

## The limits

- **A socket of your own** — subclass `TenantEventsConsumer` and mount it under `token_auth(...)` — house rule 58 (`apps/realtime/consumers.py:335`)
- **The host decides the sections** — a socket on a surface hears only the sections that surface exposes (`apps/realtime/consumers.py:625`)

Not covered here: `push_event` (the bridge's own call — a product emits). Every name: [`pilecap.realtime`](pilecap.realtime.md).
